title: Cooling specifications — 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT
introduction:
I check the engine configuration before reaching for a capacity figure: the base engine and Performance Package engine have distinct entries within the fluid rows. Treat that qualifier like the size on a socket—nearly right still belongs back in the drawer.

Use the product description, identifier and specification together, keeping original fluids separate from service materials. Read capacities in the displayed volume units, coolant-to-distilled-water percentages in that order, and pressure and temperature values with their accompanying units. This reference helps select specifications; it does not teach coolant mixing, changeover, filling, pressure testing or thermostat testing, or establish permission to mix coolant types.

edits.why: Match the original product entry first, then select the base-engine or Performance Package capacity within that row. Concentrated and prediluted products are identified separately; a listed capacity is not, by itself, an instruction for preparing coolant.

Keep the product identity and specification together, and retain the engine-configuration qualifier when reading capacity. The flushing material has its own row; the dash supplies no fill quantity. This service listing does not describe how to change from the original coolant.

The percentage pair gives coolant first and distilled water second. Read across to the corresponding freeze-protection temperature, keeping its unit attached. The extreme-cold designation applies to its row rather than to every mixture listed.

Select by the named application: complete cooling system, pressure-relief cap or radiator removed from the vehicle. A system maximum and a removed-component test pressure serve different purposes. The correct pressure value still requires the matching test setup and method.

The thermostat is the temperature-operated valve controlling the radiator route. Its initial opening and fully open condition are distinct milestones. I keep those labels attached to their temperatures instead of treating either entry as a universal engine operating temperature.
